bib.title: WebRL: Training LLM Web Agents via Self-Evolving Online Curriculum Reinforcement Learning

question: How can open LLMs be trained into strong web agents with online RL when training tasks are scarce, rewards are sparse, and the policy drifts?
hypothesis: A self-evolving curriculum, a learned outcome reward model and KL-constrained off-policy updates with a filtered replay buffer give consistent continual improvement over imitation learning and fixed-task RL (DigiRL, AWR).
contributions: WebRL: self-evolving online curriculum RL framework with RL infrastructure in WebArena and a strong ORM
Addresses task scarcity, sparse feedback and distribution drift
SOTA on WebArena-Lite, beating AWR, DigiRL and proprietary APIs

method.summary: SFT on WebArena-Lite, then 8 phases of online RL. Each phase: GPT-4o generates tasks from failed instructions, filtered by critic score and a feasibility prompt; the actor rolls out; an 8B ORM labels success (YES/NO); actor and critic are trained with a KL-constrained squared-error advantage loss on new rollouts plus perplexity-filtered successful replay data.
method.task: web-agent RL on WebArena (OpenStreetMap, Reddit, GitLab, CMS, OSS)

datasets.name: WebArena-Lite
datasets.size: 1,186 training samples (instruction, trajectory, reward function); 165 test tasks
datasets.source: Liu et al. 2024b; human-verified subset of WebArena
datasets.preprocessing: HTML simplified with element IDs for clickable elements

datasets.name: ORM training set
datasets.source: WebArena-Lite train set rewritten (instructions rewritten, place/product names changed) plus rollouts of WebRL and baselines, labelled by reward function

datasets.name: Generated curriculum tasks
datasets.size: 500 new instructions per phase after filtering
datasets.source: GPT-4o from failed instructions (in-breadth evolving, Xu et al. 2023)
datasets.preprocessing: critic scores between 0.05 and 0.75; GPT-4o feasibility filter (Fig 22)

models.name: Critic
models.architecture: SFT model plus randomly initialised value head, cross-entropy loss

models.name: ORM
models.architecture: LLM emitting YES/NO; compares P(YES) vs P(NO)
models.context: input: instruction, action history, HTML of final state only

training.objective: Actor: L=E[(beta*log(pi_theta/pi_ref) - A)^2] (off-policy, KL-constrained); critic: binary cross-entropy to final reward; advantage A = lambda*(r+gamma*V(s')-V(s)) + (1-lambda)*(gamma^(T-t)*r_T - V(s))
training.lr_schedule: WebRL constant; SFT cosine; ORM cosine
training.epochs: actor 1, critic 1 per phase; SFT 1; ORM 4
training.regularisation: KL to previous-phase policy; replay history capped at 2x new interaction data

other.beta: swept 0.01 to 10 in Fig 7; value used in main results not stated

inference.prompting: Simple prompt (Fig 21) for GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o and untuned Llama; trained agents see instruction, action history, simplified HTML

metrics.name: Success rate (SR)
metrics.definition: Fraction of 165 WebArena-Lite tasks completed per the reward function, per site and averaged

metrics.name: ORM accuracy
metrics.definition: Agreement with reward function labels (test set) or manual labels (100 rollouts)

eval.protocol: Eval after phase 8; single reported number in Table 1; 4 seeds only in Fig 13; no significance test

prompts.text: You are an expert in evaluating the performance of a website navigation agent. The agent is designed to help a human user navigate the website to complete a task. Given the user's intent, the agent's action history, and the final state of the screen, your goal is to decide whether the agent's execution is successful or not. You must respond with YES or NO.
You are a smart task creator for a website intelligent assistant. ... #Given Task# {task examples} #Created Task#

limits: Single-run Table 1 numbers on 165 tasks; seed variance only shown in Fig 13 and is larger with curriculum (task-generation randomness).
Needs GPT-4o for task generation and filtering, and an ORM trained on 12,200 reward-labelled samples from WebArena-Lite whose reward functions exist only for these tasks.
Map performance rises then declines over phases, a trade-off with OSS/CMS (App C).
Compute, hardware, beta for main runs and max steps not stated.
Evaluated on WebArena only; RL baselines other than DigiRL are offline on first-phase data.
Performance gap to WebPilot+GPT-4o (37.2%, full WebArena) not directly comparable (different test set).
